title: Alignment of NCERT Syllabus with National Education Policy 2020
body_text:
As per the recommendations of National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, the National  Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT) has brought out the National Curriculum  Framework for Foundational Stage (NCF-FS) 2022 and the National Curriculum Framework for  School Education (NCF-SE) 2023. These frameworks provide the basis for stage-wise and subject wise curricular goals, competencies, learning outcomes, syllabi, textbooks, pedagogy and  assessment.
For developing National Curriculum Frameworks, National Steering Committee was constituted  which followed bottom -up approach of seeking inputs for the National Curriculum Frameworks  from diverse stakeholders including teachers, parents, students, educational institutions, neo- and  non- literates, subjects’ experts, scholars, Anganwadi personnel etc., from across the states and UTs,  a massive process of public consultations in face-to-face as well as digital mode was conducted.  This process had benefited from the engagement of over 13 lakh interested citizens including  students and parents at the national level through citizen-centric mobile app survey and over 1.5  lakh teachers, parents, students, and educationists at the state level through mobile app survey.
Over 1550 district-level consultations in 32 States and Union Territories were conducted. Inputs  were also received from 35 groups of institutions, 8000 stakeholders who attended 12 consultations  with Universities and Civil Society Groups. More than 600 position papers on 25 specifically  relevant themes written by Focus Groups constituted by the States and UTs which all together had  over 4000 experts, and 25 papers from the National Focus Groups by expert groups with over 175  members, constituted by the NCERT. These inputs were analyzed and relevant suggestions were  included in the NCFs. Taking cognizance of these inputs, the NCF-FS was released on 20th October,  2022 and NCF-SE was released on 23rd August, 2023.
As a follow-up of the NCFs, NCERT has constituted National Syllabus and Teaching-Learning  Material Committee (NSTC). Under this Committee, 13 Curricular Area Groups (CAGs) and  Textbook Development Teams (TDTs) for all the subjects and grades have been set up. NSTC has  been assigned the task of development of teaching-learning material including textbooks. NCERT  has also constituted National Curriculum Framework Oversight Committee (NOC) to look into the  translation of NCF perspective in the new teaching-learning material including textbooks. NSTC,  NOC and CAG include scholars, subject experts, renowned players, artists, teacher educators,  faculty members of NCERT, officials from SCERTs, etc. TDT includes scholars, subject experts,  teachers, teacher educators, faculty members of NCERT, faculty members from SCERTs, etc. With  the support of NSTC, NCERT has brought out new syllabus and textbooks for Grades 1-9 and also  a collection of learning resources- Jaadui Pitara and e Jaadui Pitara for Balvatika 1, 2, and 3.
New teaching-learning material including textbooks and learning material are developed through  detailed mapping of curricular goals, competencies and learning outcomes. The drafts undergo  multiple rounds of academic, pedagogical, language and sensitivity review. The review process  examines academic accuracy, age-appropriateness, inclusivity, constitutional values, gender  sensitivity, cultural and linguistic relevance, pedagogical suitability and alignment with NEP 2020,  NCF-FS 2022 and NCF-SE 2023. As a follow-up of the NCF-SE, Learning Outcome Document and  Mandate Documents were developed, which served as guidelines for the development of new syllabi  and textbooks along with NCF-FS and NCF-SE.
NCERT, while reprinting its textbooks, every year, updates its textbooks in alignment with the  relevant feedback from students, teachers and other stakeholders, without making any structural  changes. For this purpose, also, if required, NCERT invites experts for finalizing the changes.
This information was given by the Minister of State for Education, Shri Jayant Chaudhary , in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.
***
RRTN

enrichment.summary: In a written Lok Sabha reply, Minister of State for Education Jayant Chaudhary detailed how NCERT has aligned school curricula with NEP 2020 through the National Curriculum Frameworks for Foundational Stage (2022) and School Education (2023). These frameworks emerged from extensive stakeholder consultations, and NCERT subsequently set up committees (NSTC, NOC, CAGs, TDTs) to develop new textbooks and learning material for Grades 1-9, including resources like Jaadui Pitara.
enrichment.context:
The National Education Policy 2020 mandated a fundamental restructuring of India's school education system, including a shift to a 5+3+3+4 curricular structure and a complete overhaul of curriculum, pedagogy, and assessment. NCERT, the apex body for curriculum development in India, was tasked with translating NEP's vision into concrete frameworks and materials. The National Curriculum Framework for Foundational Stage (NCF-FS, 2022) covers ages 3-8 (pre-school to Grade 2), while the National Curriculum Framework for School Education (NCF-SE, 2023) covers the entire school stage, replacing earlier frameworks like NCF 2005. These frameworks emphasize competency-based learning, foundational literacy and numeracy, Indian knowledge systems, and multilingualism.

The scale of consultation described—involving over 13 lakh citizens, 1,550+ district-level consultations, and thousands of experts—reflects the government's emphasis on a participatory, bottom-up approach to policy implementation, a hallmark claimed for NEP 2020. The institutional architecture created (NSTC, NOC, CAGs, TDTs) shows how curriculum frameworks are operationalized into actual textbooks, a process that has drawn public attention and occasional controversy over content changes in NCERT textbooks. Jaadui Pitara, a play-based early learning resource kit for the foundational stage, is a flagship NEP implementation product for Anganwadis and pre-primary classes.

prelims_questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding National Curriculum Frameworks developed under NEP 2020:
1. The National Curriculum Framework for Foundational Stage (NCF-FS) was released in 2022.
2. The National Curriculum Framework for School Education (NCF-SE) was released in 2023.
3. Both frameworks were developed exclusively by the Ministry of Education without stakeholder consultation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
prelims_questions.explanation: As per the release, NCF-FS was released on 20 October 2022 and NCF-SE on 23 August 2023. Both were developed through extensive stakeholder consultations involving citizens, teachers, parents, and experts, making statement 3 incorrect.

prelims_questions.question: 'Jaadui Pitara', mentioned in the context of NEP 2020 implementation, is best described as:
options: A national scholarship scheme for foundational stage students
A collection of play-based learning resources for Balvatika/pre-primary stages
A digital app for teacher recruitment
A financial assistance scheme for Anganwadi workers
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states that NCERT brought out Jaadui Pitara and e-Jaadui Pitara as a collection of learning resources for Balvatika 1, 2, and 3, aligned with the foundational stage curriculum framework.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of the National Curriculum Frameworks (NCF-FS 2022 and NCF-SE 2023) in operationalizing the vision of the National Education Policy 2020. Examine the institutional mechanisms created for translating these frameworks into textbooks and teaching-learning material.
mains_questions.gs_paper: GS Paper 2 - Governance and Social Justice

mains_questions.question: Stakeholder consultation is often cited as essential for effective policy implementation in education. Critically evaluate the consultative process adopted by NCERT in developing the National Curriculum Frameworks under NEP 2020, and discuss its implications for curriculum legitimacy and effectiveness.
